verdict.rationale: cubic documents natural-language operation in PR comments: users tag @cubic-dev-ai or reply to its comments to ask questions, trigger reviews and request fixes, and plain-language replies teach it what to do differently. Through its MCP server, a coding agent can also request reviews, triage issues, and manage subscriptions and seats by conversational request. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the natural-language command experience, and evidence that configuration such as cubic.yaml and rules can be changed by natural-language command rather than file/UI edits.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Interact with cubic in PR comments to ask questions, trigger reviews, and fix issues. You can tag `@cubic-dev-ai` directly, or reply to cubic's existing comments to continue the conversation.
Reply to its comments: Type a response explaining what cubic should do differently, and it remembers for next time
You can now ask your coding agent to check your cubic subscription, manage team seats and roles, and purchase more seats without leaving your MCP client.
cubic's MCP server lets your coding agent read review findings, look up codebase documentation, request PR reviews, triage PR or codebase scan issues
